I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation. That is the system I know best, it fits my land and water conditions, and it spreads labor across the year. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already the main crop on the ground, and after harvest I will plant summer maize right away to catch the heat and rainfall. I will keep the whole farm in grain rather than scatter land into too many crops, because with my age, schooling, and labor limits, I would rather do a familiar system well than take on a complicated plan.

For management, I will keep it practical. For wheat, I will use improved seed, plough before the season, apply moderate nitrogen with supporting phosphorus and potassium, irrigate at the key stages, and spray only when disease, weeds, or insects justify it. After wheat harvest, I will quickly prepare the field with rotary tillage and sow hybrid summer maize for higher yield and stronger uniformity. Maize will get a little more nitrogen than wheat, fewer irrigations if rain is normal, and a couple of pesticide rounds if armyworm, borers, or leaf disease show up. I am choosing this plan because it is the safest way for me to protect output and cash income in a normal year.
